title: Fine monoschemes, toric realization and normalized toric towers
statement:
Use the fine monoids, monoid spectra, local homomorphisms, coherent monoid ideals and saturation of [def-trf-fine-fan-blowup]. A fine monoscheme $(M,\mathcal M)$ is a space with a sheaf of commutative monoids locally isomorphic to the unsharpened spectrum $(\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}P,\widetilde P)$, whose sections on $D(a)$ are $P[a^{-1}]$. Its morphisms induce local homomorphisms on stalks. It is torsion free when all stalk group completions are torsion free. Only objects with finite affine covers are considered here. Its sharpening $M^\sharp$ replaces $\mathcal M$ by $\mathcal M/\mathcal M^\times$. A monoscheme morphism is smooth if every stalk map extends to an isomorphism $P\oplus\mathbf N^r\oplus\mathbf Z^t\simeq Q$ for finite $r,t\ge0$. The monoscheme is smooth if its stalks have this form over the zero monoid.

For a field $k$, the toric realization $k[M]$ is obtained by gluing $\operatorname{Spec}k[P]$ on the affine charts, using monoid localization on overlaps [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Here $k[P]$ is the ring of finite formal sums $\sum a_pe^p$ with $e^pe^q=e^{p+q}$. For a coherent monoid ideal $I$, $k[I]$ is the sheaf of ring ideals generated by the monomials with exponents in $I$. On each torsion-free connected component, the generic group $L=\mathcal M_\eta$ defines the split torus $T=\operatorname{Spec}k[L]$ acting by the coaction $e^p\mapsto e^p\otimes e^p$. An ideal is $T$-equivariant if its pullbacks by action and projection to $T\times_k k[M]$ agree.

Monoscheme saturated blowups have unsharpened charts $\operatorname{Spec}_{\rm mon}(P[I-a])^{\rm sat}$, in the group $P^{\rm gp}$, glued along localizations. Towers, ordered centers, pullbacks and contraction have the same recursive meanings as for fans. For a reduced toric scheme $X$, a normalized blowup along a coherent ring ideal $J$ is $\operatorname{Bl}_J(X)^\nu\to X$. The ordinary blowup has affine charts $A[J/a]\subset A_a$; normalization takes integral closure in the function field on each integral component [def-sc-normalization]. A normalized tower retains these ideal centers, pulls them back recursively along smooth maps of schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and in a contracted pullback omits a unit-ideal stage only when its normalized blowup morphism is an isomorphism; a nontrivial normalization stage is retained. A desingularization tower has a regular last scheme [def-weil-regular-scheme].

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned definition in two places. The torus clause now applies only to each torsion-free connected component, as required by ILO VIII 3.2.4; the torsion example P=Z/2 over Q gives μ₂ rather than a split torus. The normalized-tower contraction clause now omits a unit-ideal stage only when its normalized blowup map is an isomorphism, retaining nontrivial normalization such as Spec Q[t] → Spec Q[t²,t³]. Re-read ILO VIII 2.2.3--2.2.8, 2.3.4, 3.1.9--3.1.22 and 3.2.1--3.2.15, all five dependency statements, and reran the changed Mathlib searches; no child nodes are needed because this remains a definition.
